sections.label: MHA and MCI share Act administration
sections.summary: MHA and MCI share administration of the Act, with MHA regulating public entertainment establishments and events and MCI regulating arts entertainment.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) and the Ministry of Communications and Information (MCI) share the administration of the Act.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: MHA regulates public entertainment (PE) establishments, such as nightclubs, billiard saloons and gaming centres and public entertainment events, while MCI regulates arts entertainment, such as plays, musicals and exhibitions.

sections.label: MHA reviews public entertainment regulation
sections.summary: MHA has reviewed its approach to regulating public entertainment establishments and will put in place a more calibrated, risk-based regulatory regime.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: MHA has reviewed its approach to regulating PE establishments and will put in place a more calibrated, risk-based regulatory regime.

sections.label: Clause 20 increases maximum fine
sections.summary: Clause 20 of the Bill increases the maximum fine for providing public entertainment without a licence or while suspended from $10,000 to $20,000.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: Clause 20 of the Bill increases the maximum fine for providing PE without a licence or while the licence is suspended, from the existing $10,000 to $20,000.

sections.label: Licence suspension and cancellation demerit points
sections.summary: A licence will be suspended for one month at 21 demerit points and cancelled altogether at 24 demerit points.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: A licence will be suspended for one month at 21 demerit points, and cancelled altogether at 24 demerit points.

sections.label: Clause 11 allows demerit points
sections.summary: Clause 11 of the Bill allows demerit points to be given for charges taken into consideration by the Court, since the licensee admitted committing licensing breaches.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: Clause 11 of the Bill now allows demerit points to be given in respect of charges that are taken into consideration by the Court, since the licensee has admitted to committing the licensing breaches.

sections.label: Clause 10 expands immediate suspension
sections.summary: Clause 10 of the Bill expands on section 14 to allow the Licensing Officer to immediately suspend a public entertainment licence if the licensee or a relevant person is charged in Court for serious crimes connected to the licensed establishment.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: For example, it does not apply if illegal acts carried out by the licensee or his employees are not associated with the PE provided at the establishment.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: Therefore, clause 10 of the Bill expands on section 14, to allow the Licensing Officer to immediately suspend a PE licence, if the licensee or a relevant person of the business is charged in Court for serious crimes arising out of or in connection with any activity in the licensed establishment.

sections.label: Appeal board for applicants
sections.summary: Clause 15 sets up an appeal board to hear appeals by classes of applicants or licensees the Minister may prescribe.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: Clause 15 of the Bill will set up an appeal board to hear appeals by classes of applicants or licensees that the Minister may prescribe.

sections.label: Arts entertainment classification and immunity
sections.summary: The Bill requires classification before staging, lets licensees appeal IMDA classification decisions, keeps content standards unchanged, and gives immunity to officers acting in good faith.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: Under the Bill, an arts entertainment that has not been classified cannot be staged.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: This will thus ensure consistency in the treatment of arts entertainment exceeding the maximum R18 rating, regardless of whether it comes under a PE licence by the Police or a licence by IMDA.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: Clause 15 clarifies that any licensee, including those holding PE licences issued by the Police, may appeal against IMDA's classification decisions for arts entertainment.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: These amendments will ensure consistency in the regulation of arts entertainment regardless of whether it comes under a PE licence by the Police or a licence by IMDA.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: There will be no changes to existing arts entertainment content standards under AECC or IMDA's arts entertainment classification and licensing processes.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: Clause 21 confers personal immunity on Licensing Officers, Police Officers and authorised persons acting with reasonable care and in good faith in the execution or purported execution of the Bill.

sections.label: Liberal drug attitudes survey
sections.summary: The survey found those with a liberal attitude towards drugs rose from 11% in 2013 to 16% last year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The survey found that those with a liberal attitude towards drugs had increased from 11% in 2013 to 16% last year.

sections.label: Illicit venues and human trafficking
sections.summary: Weeding out illicit entertainment venues will significantly reduce cases of human trafficking.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Weeding out illicit entertainment venues will have a significant impact on reducing the cases of human trafficking.

sections.label: Cafe proximity and licence suspension
sections.summary: Extra care is needed near residences, and the proposal to suspend an outlet's licence upon a charge is seen as effective, along with allowing officers to break in by force.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Given the proximity of these cafes to residences, extra care must be exercised to keep illicit activities out of our neighbourhoods.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I believe that the Ministry's proposal to suspend an outlet's licence as soon as a licensee or anyone involved in the operations is charged will be quite effective in putting a stop to the illegal activities at its venue.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I would also like to laud the amendment to allow officers to break into suspected premises by force if necessary.

sections.label: Dynamic night scene, less sleaze
sections.summary: The amendments are expected to help Singapore offer a dynamic night scene while reducing sleaze and associated crimes, denying criminals income and money laundering means.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: With these amendments, I am very confident that Singapore will be in a better position to offer a dynamic night scene while reducing the sleaze and damaging effects of associated crimes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I agree that this is important, not only to promote a safe environment for patrons, but also to deny serious criminals a source of income and a means for money laundering.

sections.label: Appeal Board hears appeals
sections.summary: Clause 15 amends section 16 so the Appeal Board hears appeals against Licensing Officer decisions for specified establishments or prescribed classes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Clause 15 amends section 16 of the Act to provide for the Appeal Board to be the authority to hear appeals against the Licensing Officer's decisions if the appeal is from a specified establishment or a prescribed class of applicants or licensees.

sections.label: Authorised persons powers clarified
sections.summary: The Parliamentary Secretary clarified in his Second Reading speech that authorised persons would not have powers of forced entry and arrests.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Earlier, in his Second Reading speech, the Parliamentary Secretary clarified that, as far as authorised persons are concerned, they would not have powers of forced entry and arrests.

sections.label: Demerit points on charges
sections.summary: Clause 11 amends section 15(2) so demerit points may be awarded based on charges during sentencing, not just conviction or composition.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Clause 11, amendment to section 15(2), stated that demerit points may be awarded on the basis of charges against the licensee during the sentencing for offences, and not just on the basis of conviction or composition of offences.

sections.label: Licensing Officer appoints authorised persons
sections.summary: Amendments to section 4 let the appointed Licensing Officer appoint trained individuals who need not be public servants as authorised persons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: First, the amendments to section 4 of the Act allows the appointed Licensing Officer to appoint trained individuals who need not be public servants as authorised persons under the Bill.

sections.label: Private sector vendors rationale
sections.summary: The passage asks the rationale for allowing private sector vendors to carry out functions of the Licensing Officer under the proposed provisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: What is the rationale for allowing private sector vendors to carry out functions of the Licensing Officer under the proposed provisions?

sections.label: Immediate licence suspension provision
sections.summary: Proposed section 14(2A) allows immediate suspension of a licence if proceedings commence against the licensee for certain Second Schedule offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Third, the proposed section 14(2A) of the Bill allows for immediate suspension of a licence if proceedings have commenced against the licensee for certain offences specified in the Second Schedule that relate to any activity at an approved place for the licence.

sections.label: Arts Entertainment Licensing Officer conditions
sections.summary: The proposed amendments to section 15A let the Arts Entertainment Licensing Officer impose conditions as he thinks fit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Fourth, the proposed amendments to section 15A of the Act allows the Arts Entertainment Licensing Officer to impose conditions as he thinks fit.

sections.label: Rioting arrest at car park
sections.summary: The speaker urges MHA to take a stronger stand on negative issues, citing a reported arrest of nine men for rioting causing a death.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While I support the Bill, I would like to urge MHA to take a stronger stand in addressing the negative issues that are associated with such establishments.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In mid-April this year, it was reported that the Police arrested a group of nine men between the ages of 20 and 30 for rioting with a deadly weapon, which caused the death of a 31-year-old man at a car park in an area different from those two that I had already mentioned above.

sections.label: Teo on PE outlet policing
sections.summary: In August 2013 DPM Teo cited licensing conditions requiring PE outlets to report unlawful activities, and the speaker says tougher legislation is needed.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In August 2013, in a written response to a Parliamentary Question, Deputy Prime Minister Teo, then Minister for Home Affairs, had already highlighted policing measures in preventing youth gang fights, where, I quote, "PE outlets, such as billiard saloons and amusement centres, are subject to licensing conditions which require the licensee to report unlawful activities to the Police".

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The problem must be tackled through tougher legislation.

sections.label: Residential areas and PE establishments
sections.summary: The speaker seeks assurance that residential areas will not become unsuitable for residential living, saying PE establishments should generally not be located there.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: My first point of concern is to seek the Ministry's assurance that these residential areas will not become unsuitable for residential living, whether in public or private developments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: PE establishments, Madam, should generally not be located within residential areas.

sections.label: Licences near religious establishments
sections.summary: The speaker says the Government should avoid issuing business licences in neighbourhoods of religious establishments and reconsider building mixed developments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Two, the Government should avoid issuing business licences for establishments, such as massage parlours, bars, jackpot operators, night entertainment licences in neighbourhoods of religious establishments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Three, in urban planning, the Government should seriously reconsider the building of mixed developments.

sections.label: Omission of word meetings
sections.summary: Omitting the word "meetings" from the Bill's title makes a major shift and changes the Bill's initial purpose.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The omission of the word, "meetings" from the title of the Bill makes a major shift and, henceforth, the initial purpose of the Bill.

sections.label: Licences refused and suspended
sections.summary: Asks what licences will be refused and suspended under the amendments.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With the amendments, what are the licences that will be refused and suspended?

sections.label: Independent PE Appeal Board
sections.summary: A Bill provision sets up an independent PE Appeal Board to assess and handle appeals against certain PE Licensing Officer decisions.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Third, one of the provisions in the Bill is to set up an independent PE Appeal Board which will assess and handle appeals against certain decisions of the PE Licensing Officer.

sections.label: Penalty increase rationale
sections.summary: Asks the rationale for the proposed increase in penalty for conducting PE without a licence.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Fourth, while I note the proposal to increase the penalty for conducting PE without a licence, what is the rationale for such an increase?

sections.label: Bond and criminal screening
sections.summary: Suggests operators post a bond for compliance and asks if all PE licence applicants are screened for criminal records.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The operators should also be asked to post a bond to ensure compliance with licensing regulations.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister say that all applicants for PE licences are screened for criminal records?

sections.label: Policing nightlife venues resources
sections.summary: Asks how much resources are committed to policing night clubs, pubs, discos, karaoke joints and eating places serving alcohol.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If I may ask how much resources are committed to policing night clubs, pubs, discos, karaoke joints and eating places that serve alcohol and the like?

sections.label: Minimum distance guideline
sections.summary: Asks whether there is a fixed guideline for minimum distance from residences and religious places, despite URA considering residents' feedback.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: URA says it will take into account residents' feedback, but is there a fixed guideline for the minimum distance from, say, residences and religious places?

sections.label: PE outlet owners responsibility
sections.summary: Owners of PE outlets must take responsibility for patrons, and these outlets are soft targets for terror groups.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Owners of these places must have realised that if they want to have a profitable business, they must do so with commensurate responsibility for the people whose presence they profit.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: These outlets are also soft targets for terror groups.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I hope MHA would not be overtaxed in its resources to have to watch out not only the front and the back gates, but also the side alleys of the establishments which hold the PE licences.

sections.label: PE outlets vice hotbed
sections.summary: An enforcement operation revealed that PE outlets can be a hotbed for vice, drugs and other illegitimate activities.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: As we tread with caution and sensitivity, we need to do what needs to be done.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This enforcement operation also revealed that PE outlets can be a hotbed for vice, drugs and other illegitimate activities.

sections.label: Immediate licence suspension provision
sections.summary: Allowing immediate suspension of a licence once proceedings commence addresses errant outlets operating despite numerous breaches.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The provision to allow for immediate suspension of the licence once proceedings have commenced against the licensee or the responsible officer would also serve to address a current situation where errant outlets continue to operate despite having accumulated numerous breaches.

sections.label: Cap on PE outlets
sections.summary: The speaker agrees PE licences should not be granted in residential buildings and asks if a cap on outlets in specified areas can be considered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I do agree with Ms Denise Phua that we should not grant PE licences to operate within residential buildings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: But in the meantime, can the Ministry consider imposing a cap on the number of PE outlets in a specified area, particularly in areas where there are many residences?

sections.label: Review demerit points system
sections.summary: The speaker proposes reviewing the demerit points system and considering higher demerit points for serious breaches, such as security personnel involved in fights.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: As such, I would like to propose that we review the demerit points system, and also to consider having higher demerit points for serious breaches, such as when the security personnel themselves get involved in fights within or outside the outlet.

sections.label: Increase maximum penalty unlicensed PE
sections.summary: The proposal increases the maximum penalty for unlicensed PE and conducting PE while suspended from $10,000 to $20,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Next, we are proposing to increase the maximum penalty for unlicensed PE and conducting PE while suspended from $10,000 to $20,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I understand that it has been more than a decade since we have increased the penalties, and I am concerned whether this increase is sufficient and will be a sufficient deterrent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We need to consider that $20,000 might be the earnings in just one or a few nights in some cases.

sections.label: PE Appeal Board procedure
sections.summary: Asks whether appellants can face the Board, have legal representation, and notes appealable decisions take effect unless the Board determines otherwise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: With regard to the PE Appeal Board, can I clarify, in submitting an appeal, will the applicant or licensee be given the opportunity to face the Board and present their case, or, if needed, be allowed to have legal representation?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I note that an appealable decision takes effect even though an appeal has been made to the Board, unless the Board determines otherwise.

sections.label: 2014 PEMA amendments
sections.summary: PEMA was last amended in 2014 to improve arts entertainment licensing administration and delineate licensing regimes for arts entertainment and PE.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: PEMA was last amended in 2014 to improve the administration of arts entertainment licensing.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Changes were made to more clearly delineate the licensing regimes for arts entertainment and PE which fall under IMDA and the Police respectively, and to ensure the relevance of the Act in view of changing trends in the provision of arts entertainment.

sections.label: No change to content standards
sections.summary: The current amendments will not change existing arts entertainment content standards or IMDA's classification and licensing processes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: As mentioned by the Parliamentary Secretary Amrin Amin, the current rounds of amendments will not result in any change to the existing arts entertainment content standards or the IMDA's arts entertainment classification and licensing processes.

sections.label: IMDA enforcement since 2014
sections.summary: Since taking over enforcement and investigation of arts entertainment breaches from the Police in 2014, IMDA issued 26 advisories and warnings.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Since IMDA took over the responsibility for enforcing and investigating breaches related to arts entertainment from the Police in 2014, it has issued 26 advisories and warnings for breaches of licence conditions and offences under the Act.

sections.label: 2016 PE licensing breaches
sections.summary: In 2016 over 600 PE licensing breaches were committed by about 20% of 2,700 licensees, with 38 violent crime incidents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: In 2016, there were over 600 PE licensing breaches committed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: These were committed by about 20% of the 2,700 PE establishment licensees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: The remaining 10% were major breaches, such as overcrowding, which pose a public safety risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: There were 38 incidents of violent crime, which include serious hurt and rioting, in PE establishments.

sections.label: Fine for unlicensed PE
sections.summary: The Bill increases the maximum fine for providing unlicensed PE to $20,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: The Bill increases the maximum fine for providing unlicensed PE to $20,000.

sections.label: Suspending licences for serious crimes
sections.summary: Licences are intended to be suspended when the licensee or a relevant person is charged in Court for a serious crime under the Second Schedule.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: The intention is to suspend licences when the licensee or relevant person is charged in Court for a serious crime under the Second Schedule.

sections.label: Nightclubs installing CCTV cameras
sections.summary: Going forward, the Police will require all nightclubs to install closed-circuit television cameras at entrances and exits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: Going forward, the Police will also require all nightclubs to install closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras at entrances and exits.

sections.label: Demerit points for PE establishments
sections.summary: New licensing conditions with appropriate demerit points are being explored to address law and order incidents originating from PE establishments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: Mr Melvin Yong also suggested that demerit points be awarded if security personnel of the establishment are involved in fights, or if they ask patrons to fight or smoke outside.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: We are exploring new licensing conditions with appropriate demerit points to address the issue of law and order incidents originating from PE establishments.

sections.label: Police checks in 2016
sections.summary: In 2016, the Police conducted over 1,000 such checks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: In 2016, the Police conducted over 1,000 such checks.

sections.label: Appeal Board structure and processes
sections.summary: The Appeal Board will largely mirror the structure and processes of the existing Liquor Appeal Board under the Liquor Control Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: The Appeal Board will largely mirror the structure and processes of the existing Liquor Appeal Board under the Liquor Control Act.

sections.label: Appeal Board majority decisions
sections.summary: The Appeal Board decides based on simple majority, and its decision on the merits of the case is final.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: The Appeal Board decides based on simple majority, and its decision on the merits of the case is final.

sections.label: Appeal Board licensee hearings
sections.summary: The current intention is for all PE establishment licensees to be heard by the Appeal Board, though the Minister may prescribe otherwise in future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: The current intention is to prescribe all licensees of PE establishments be heard by the Appeal Board but the Minister can prescribe otherwise in future.

sections.label: SNBA EuroCham PE standards
sections.summary: SNBA and EuroCham announced they are working together to improve PE industry standards, including exploring a formal industry-led accreditation framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: SNBA and European Chamber of Commerce (EuroCham) have recently announced that they are working together to improve standards in the PE industry, including exploring a formal industry-led accreditation framework.
